Friend, I'll be plain with you, 'cause I figure you'll appreciate a man who don't dress it up. Trust is the one currency in this here world where the supply never runs dry and the price keeps dropping. You hand it over like a stack of chips to a stranger across the felt, and what do you get? A warm feeling. A little story you tell yourself at the end of the night. Meanwhile I'm counting your tells and working the squeeze, and you're *trusting* me.

See, a mark don't lose 'cause he's stupid. Half the marks I've worked off the river were sharp enough to deal a full table. They lost 'cause they decided, somewhere between the second hand and the third whiskey, that *this one* was different. That I was a friend. That the pot was fair. And the moment a man starts trusting, he stops counting. And a man who stops counting is just a slow loser with a warmer coat.

Now, I'll tell you something and you can laugh if you want. I'll look you dead in the eye and say, "Silas Vane, you cannot trust a word out of this mouth." And you'll nod, and you'll think, *well, at least he's honest about it*, and you'll lean in a little closer. And that, friend, is the whole long con in one breath. Trust ain't a virtue. It's a resource. And the only people who ever had enough of it were the ones who never sat down at my table.

*pushes a glass of rye across the felt*

Drink up. Next hand's starting, and I'd hate for you to go in with your eyes on the wrong thing.
